facts.text: Blue Flag beach, patrolled by lifeguards during summer months; licensed bar/restaurant concessions, toilets, showers, parasol and sun-lounger rental.
Bordered on the north by the Ribeira da Granja stream; Espinho lies to the south, Porto/Gaia to the north.

Name derives from a bishop's farm ("quinta") built on the site in 1758, later known as Quinta da Granja / Quinta dos Ayres / Quinta do Bispo, used by Crúzios monks from the Grijó monastery as a rest retreat in hot weather.
Also historically known as "Praia da Meia Laranja."

On 7 September 1876, leaders of Portugal's Partido Histórico and Partido Reformista signed a fusion agreement here — the "Pacto da Granja" — creating the Partido Progressista under Anselmo José Braamcamp.

Poet Sophia de Mello Breyner Andresen summered at a family beach house here and wrote verses about it: "A casa branca, em frente ao mar, enorme, / com o teu jardim de areia e flores marinhas / e o teu silêncio intocado em que dorme / o milagre das coisas minhas."

Fine, extensive sand; north and central zones less frequented due to rocky outcrops in the water; a viewpoint (miradouro) near the end of the bike path (ciclovia) on the south end; adjacent municipal swimming-pool complex (indoor + outdoor, both saltwater).
A wooden boardwalk (passadiço) runs 15 km along Vila Nova de Gaia's beaches, passing through Praia da Granja.

Academic coastal-geology literature (H. Granja et al.) treats this stretch (Foz do Douro to Praia da Granja) as a documented coastal-erosion case study, with sediment loss and paleoenvironmental reconstruction papers spanning 2000-2015.
Nearby Praia da Aguda / Praia da Granja area has cited (not fully sourced here) traces of early protohistoric human occupation.
